These laws are grounded in Gestalt principles and conditioned reflex mechanisms. The temporal ordering primitive captures the sequential nature of stimulus exposure, which is essential for learning and adaptation. The gestalt induction primitive formalizes the emergence of global patterns from local interactions. Together, these form a dual structure: one rooted in relational algebra (interrelations), the other in temporal logic (ordering). Failure modes arise when perceptual thresholds are exceeded or when relational coherence is lost. Dualities emerge between static interrelation structures and dynamic temporal sequences, enabling predictive modeling in both GSI and GSE domains.
